title: Closed-model hosting: operator separation, confidential on-prem inference and CPU demand implications
scope: Public-only multi-provider research plus indexed keynote URLs. Distinguish demonstrated deployment/products, historical commercial contracts, proposed security architecture and speculative enterprise GPT/Claude self-hosted weights. No full transcripts, no confidential client data and no inferred CPU TAM figures.

claims.statement: Claude Platform on AWS is Anthropic-operated on AWS infrastructure; Anthropic processes inference inputs/outputs while AWS integrates identity and billing.
claims.source_locator: How the platform integration works; comparison table

claims.statement: Claude in Amazon Bedrock is operated on AWS-managed infrastructure, with Anthropic personnel having no access to the inference infrastructure.
Bedrock maintains AWS-owned and operated model deployment accounts inaccessible to model providers, and deep-copies provider inference/training software into those accounts.
Google documents GDC connected as Google-managed software on customer hardware; GDC air-gapped uses Google-supplied hardware and supports disconnected deployments.

signals.statement: A single closed model is offered via different operator/control plane arrangements.
signals.inference: A model developer can separate IP ownership from the party operating the inference stack; compare product and data-processing boundaries rather than merely cloud brand.

signals.statement: Proprietary Gemini deployment is documented in customer premises under a vendor-managed software lifecycle.
signals.inference: Customer-local proprietary inference is an established vendor offering, but product model/version and hardware ownership constraints matter.

signals.statement: A reference stack protects model weights inside attested CPU/GPU execution on enterprise infrastructure.
signals.inference: Security certification, attestation/key release and OEM systems integration may become enabling supply-chain layers; commercial authorization remains distinct.

signals.statement: The April 2026 partnership amendment broadened cross-cloud delivery rights.
signals.inference: Prior Azure-exclusivity narrative must be versioned and cannot be used as a current market constraint; the amendment still does not grant bank-run GPT weights.

hypotheses.thesis: Closed-model vendors may license encrypted, nonmodifiable model runtime packages for enterprise-controlled AI factories in high-regulation/high-utilization accounts before 2030.
hypotheses.alternative: Vendors retain managed APIs because security, policy control, IP extraction risk and pooled-GPU utilization dominate enterprise demand.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Track signed OpenAI/Anthropic customer-premises inference entitlements by model/version/operator/region and verify commercial terms; distinguish sovereign managed appliances from truly customer-operated models.

hypotheses.thesis: A shift from central hyperscaler inference to private AI factories changes the entity buying CPU host silicon, its OEM channel, and ISA opportunity, but is not necessarily additive to global CPU sockets.
hypotheses.alternative: Enterprise deployment only relocates equivalent accelerator-attached CPUs already counted in cloud equipment, or increases utilization of existing enterprise compute.
hypotheses.falsification_test: For matched workloads track service buyer, physical hardware owner, CPU shipment purchaser, channel, incremental socket additions, utilization, displacement, and AMD/Intel/Arm host ISA.

hypotheses.thesis: Attested confidential inference increases demand for verified CPU-TEE platform support, OEM certification, secure-firmware operations and enterprise integration, potentially changing CPU/platform purchase criteria.
hypotheses.alternative: GPU-side confidential compute and virtualized cloud APIs capture value without a meaningful incremental x86 CPU premium.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Compare certified BOMs, CPU ISA/SKU mix, CPU attach ratio per GPU, security software costs and actual procurement contracts for private versus public inference.

questions.question: Are OpenAI or Anthropic offering any customer-controlled on-prem inference licenses for closed weights; exactly which model and hardware scope?
questions.method: Search first-party enterprise/offering docs, model entitlement matrices and public contracts; ask vendors for written deployment rights.
questions.decision_impacted: Determine whether proprietary models create a new OEM/enterprise buying channel.

questions.question: What is the net incremental server CPU silicon demand from enterprise private AI factories versus workload relocation?
questions.method: Build buyer–owner–channel event crosswalk; collect deployed system BOM/CPU socket and GPU attach factors; subtract relocated/double-counted cloud demand.
questions.decision_impacted: Protect the server CPU TAM denominator from duplicated cloud and OEM demand.

questions.question: Which shipping EPYC, Xeon and Arm host platforms are certified with NVIDIA GPU confidential computing for proprietary-model inference?
questions.method: Cross-check NVIDIA supported platform matrix, AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, BIOS/driver, ODM/OEM BOM and supply availability.
questions.decision_impacted: Assess x86 vs Arm selection pressure from mandatory TEEs.

questions.question: Where is cost-per-usable-token crossover across bank-owned, dedicated neocloud and shared hosted APIs?
questions.method: Model utilization, batching, GPU depreciation, CPU attachment, power, network, license fee, failover and service commitments; label scenarios.
questions.decision_impacted: Quantify likely private-model hosting uptake rather than infer it from announcements.

questions.question: Who controls attestation root, decryption keys, revocation, model safety updates, telemetry and disconnected operation?
questions.method: Compare Google GDC, NVIDIA CoCo, Bedrock and enterprise licensing contracts with explicit threat-model acceptance tests.
questions.decision_impacted: Assess deployability in regulated and air-gapped buyers.

questions.question: Which keynote segment claims survive comparison with official product documentation and transcribed primary recording?
questions.method: Verify each video URL and exact timestamp against publisher source; extract only authorized short quotes or normalized claims, cite the source locator.
questions.decision_impacted: Convert viewing queue into confirmed attributable evidence.

questions.question: How much physical capacity is actually provider-operated versus outsourced among frontier developers, separately for training and inference?
questions.method: Triangulate public deployment announcements, infrastructure partners and revenue relationships, classify hardware owner versus model operator.
questions.decision_impacted: Estimate addressable infrastructure OEM and neocloud opportunity without assigning training capacity to inference.

conflicts.issue: The February 27 statement's Azure-exclusive stateless API language is superseded by the April 27 announcement allowing OpenAI to serve products on any cloud and making Microsoft's IP license nonexclusive.
conflicts.resolution_plan: Preserve both dated contractual source assertions. Use April 27 amended terms as latest public position, without implying third-party weights self-host rights.

methods.name: Closed-model inference placement to CPU demand mapping
methods.procedure: For each deployment separately identify model IP owner, inference stack operator, underlying hardware owner, CPU procurement buyer, OEM/ODM channel, service subscriber, training/inference workload, accelerator host CPU ISA, physical CPU quantity, incremental versus relocated utilization, and contractual model rights. Aggregate CPU silicon once by physical purchase event; never sum OEM sales plus end buyer as two chip purchases.
assumptions: Training and inference are separate workload classes.
Signed vendor rights do not follow automatically from a hardware-hosting agreement.
Private deployment may shift purchases between buyer types without raising total unit demand.
CPU TEE support must be validated by SKU/firmware/guest/GPU configuration.
methods.notes: Implements docs/research/demand-2030/TAXONOMY-AND-ACCOUNTING.md and adds an orthogonal model control plane dimension.

handoff.summary: Observed today: AWS operates Bedrock Claude separately from Anthropic-operated Claude Platform on AWS; Gemini can be deployed on premises under defined GDC configurations; NVIDIA documents an attested encrypted proprietary-model inference architecture. April OpenAI-Microsoft terms supersede February Azure-exclusive clause. Enterprise GPT/Claude on-prem closed-weight licensing is NOT demonstrated by these sources.
